config.title: Mini Redux

intro.title: Mini Redux
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simplified version of Redux state management within an Angular application. You'll learn how to implement core Redux concepts like a central store, actions, and reducers to manage application state predictably. The main technologies involved are Angular services for the store implementation, TypeScript interfaces for action definitions, and pure functions for reducers. By the end, you'll understand how state flows unidirectionally from actions through reducers to update the store, which is a fundamental pattern in modern web development.
intro.usecase: The Redux pattern is essential for managing complex state in real-world Angular applications like e-commerce platforms, where shopping cart items, user authentication, and inventory status must stay synchronized across multiple components. In financial dashboards, Redux ensures that stock prices, portfolio balances, and transaction histories update consistently across charts, tables, and summary panels. Developers use this pattern in collaborative tools like project management apps to handle real-time changes to tasks, user assignments, and notifications without manual state propagation.

objectives: Implement a basic Redux store with state and reducer functions
Configure Angular components to dispatch actions to the store
Initialize and bind component state to the Redux store using observables
Manipulate application state by applying reducer logic to dispatched actions
Integrate Redux store updates with Angular component rendering
Construct a complete mini Redux pattern within an Angular application
Control state changes through action creators and type definitions

steps.title: Import Angular core modules and create the main component
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and create the main AppComponent with basic structure. The AppComponent should be a class with @Component decorator that includes a template with a heading for your Mini Redux app.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define your component. The template can be a simple string containing an <h1> element.

seedCode.App.tsx: // Import Component from '@angular/core' and create the AppComponent

steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic Angular component structure ready for building the Mini Redux implementation.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and AppComponent is created with @Component decorator containing a template with a heading
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've imported Component from '@angular/core' and created the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: import Component from '@angular/core' and create the AppComponent class with @Component decorator that includes a template.

steps.title: Define the state interface and initial state
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, define an interface named AppState and create an initial state object.
steps.hint: Create an interface with a property (e.g., 'count' of type number) and an object that matches that interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a typed AppState interface and an initial state object ready for the Mini Redux store.
successCriteria: AppState interface is defined with at least one property, and an initial state object matching that interface is created.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you define both the interface and the initial state object with matching properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you defined an interface named AppState and created an initial state object that implements it.

steps.title: Create action types and action interface
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, define two string constants for action types: 'INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT'.
steps.hint: Use the 'export' keyword for the interface so it can be used elsewhere. Remember TypeScript interfaces define the shape of objects.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have action type constants and a typed Action interface ready for use in the Mini Redux implementation.
successCriteria: Two string constants ('INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT') are defined, and an Action interface with 'type' and optional 'payload' properties is created.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined both action type constants ('INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT') and the Action interface with the correct properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The action types or Action interface are missing or incorrect. Check that you've defined two string constants and an interface with 'type' and optional 'payload' properties.

steps.title: create an Action interface with a 'type' prop
steps.instruction: create an Action interface with a 'type' property (string) and an optional 'payload' property (any type).
steps.hint: Use the 'export' keyword for the interface so it can be used elsewhere. Remember TypeScript interfaces define the shape of objects.
steps.feedbackPartial: Review the instruction and try again.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Implement the reducer function
steps.instruction: Create a reducer function named 'counterReducer' that takes current state and an action, and returns a new state based on the action type.
steps.hint: Define a function with two parameters: state (of type CounterState) and action (of type Action). Use a switch statement on action.type to handle different action types and return the appropriate new state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A pure reducer function that handles state transitions for increment and decrement actions.
successCriteria: The 'counterReducer' function is defined with proper TypeScript types, uses a switch statement to handle action types, and returns new state objects.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your reducer function has proper TypeScript type annotations and handles all action cases.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reducer function is missing or incorrect. Remember to create a function named 'counterReducer' that takes state and action parameters and returns new state based on action type.

steps.title: Create the Mini Redux store service
steps.instruction: Create an Angular service named StoreService with a state property, a reducer function, and a dispatch method.
steps.hint: Use the @Injectable decorator to create a service. The state property should be of type CounterState, initialized with initialState. The dispatch method should accept an Action and update state by calling the reducer.
steps.expectedOutcome: The StoreService will be created with the necessary structure to manage state using the reducer pattern.
successCriteria: StoreService is created with @Injectable, has a state property of type CounterState, and includes a dispatch method that calls counterReducer.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the service includes all required elements: @Injectable, state property, and dispatch method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The StoreService is missing or incomplete. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Initialize component state from the store
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent, inject the StoreService and initialize a component property called 'state' with the current store state.
steps.hint: Add a constructor parameter with StoreService type and assign this.store.getState() to this.state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have access to the store's current state through the injected StoreService.
successCriteria: StoreService is injected in the constructor, and the component's state property is initialized with store.getState().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've both injected the StoreService and assigned this.store.getState() to this.state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't properly connected to the store. Check that you've injected StoreService and initialized the state property.

steps.title: Create action creator functions
steps.instruction: Create two action creator functions: one named increment and one named decrement, each returning an action object with the appropriate type.
steps.hint: Define each function to return an object with a type property matching the action types you defined earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two action creator functions are defined: increment() and decrement(), each returning an action object with the correct type property.
successCriteria: The increment function returns { type: 'INCREMENT' } and the decrement function returns { type: 'DECREMENT' }.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure both functions return an object with a type property matching the action types.
steps.feedbackWrong: Action creators should be simple functions that return action objects. Check that you've defined both increment and decrement functions correctly.

steps.title: Add template structure to display state
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add a paragraph element that displays the current count from the component's state property.
steps.hint: Use Angular's interpolation syntax {{ }} to display the count value from the state object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the current count value from the component's state using Angular interpolation.
successCriteria: The AppComponent template contains a paragraph element with interpolation that displays state.count
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct property path (state.count) and Angular interpolation syntax {{ }}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the state value. Add a paragraph element with interpolation to show state.count.

steps.title: Add buttons and wire them to dispatch actions
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add two buttons with click events that dispatch the INCREMENT and DECREMENT actions using the store's dispatch method.
steps.hint: Use the store service injected in the constructor to call dispatch with the appropriate action objects.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a button click to dispatch an action
<button (click)="store.dispatch({ type: 'INCREMENT' })">Increment</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will have two buttons that, when clicked, dispatch actions to update the counter state.
successCriteria: Two buttons are added to the template with (click) events that call store.dispatch with action objects containing type 'INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added buttons, but the click events might not be correctly wired to dispatch the actions. Check that each button's (click) event calls store.dispatch with the correct action type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing or not properly wired to dispatch actions. Ensure you have two buttons with (click) events that dispatch INCREMENT and DECREMENT actions.

steps.title: Subscribe to store changes and update component
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent constructor, subscribe to the store's state changes and update the component's state property when the store state changes.
steps.hint: Call the store's getState() method to get the current state, then assign it to this.state. Use the store's stateChanges observable to subscribe and update this.state whenever the state changes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will automatically update its state whenever the store's state changes, keeping the UI in sync with the latest state.
successCriteria: The AppComponent constructor subscribes to store state changes and updates this.state when changes occur.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're subscribing to the store's stateChanges observable and updating this.state inside the subscription callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The subscription isn't set up correctly. Remember to call store.getState() to initialize this.state, then subscribe to store.stateChanges to update this.state when changes occur.
